extracted.intended_audience: general news readers and entertainment/celebrity audience
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and public reactions for judging when a comedian's onstage remarks cross the line into hate speech or dangerous rhetoric, and how employers/peers should respond. Applies to celebrity stand-up incidents and their reputational, ethical, and safety implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid violent imagery that targets marginalized groups
rubrics_metrics.description: "the violent imagery of Tracy's rant was disturbing to me at a time when homophobic hate crimes continue to be a life-threatening issue for the GLBT Community" (Tina Fey)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if used as part of a joke, violent imagery aimed at or referencing marginalized groups can be disturbing and unacceptable because it echoes real-world threats; comedians should avoid language that invokes or normalizes violence against vulnerable populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context does not automatically excuse reckless statements
rubrics_metrics.description: "We will always recognize an artist's freedom to express him or herself, but not when reckless things are said no matter what the context." (NBC's Bob Greenblatt)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artistic freedom to 'work out' material exists, but context (e.g., a comedy club) does not absolve speakers of responsibility when speech is reckless or harmful; assess both intent and potential harm rather than relying solely on performance context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider real-world repercussions and harm to youth
rubrics_metrics.description: "The devastating repercussions of hate-filled language manifest in very real ways for today's LGBTQ youth." (Cheyenne Jackson) and Wanda Sykes: "Tracy just yelled, 'Fire,' in a crowded theater."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether remarks could contribute to stigma, bullying, or violence against youth and other vulnerable people. Speech that increases risk or normalizes hostility toward a group is especially problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance free speech with community standards and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: "I do believe in free speech, but ... Tracy has the right to say whatever he wants to say, just like we have the right to say, not acceptable...This isn't about comedy. What Tracy said is dangerous." (Wanda Sykes)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge comedians' free-speech rights while also holding them accountable to community standards; the existence of free expression does not preclude public criticism or professional consequences when speech endangers others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity and acceptability of apology matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple voices: Tina Fey: "I hope for his sake that Tracy's apology will be accepted as sincere by his gay and lesbian coworkers..." Cheyenne Jackson: "hope that his apology is sincere."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When offensive remarks are followed by apologies, evaluate the apology's sincerity and whether affected communities accept it. A genuine apology may mitigate harm; an insincere one can exacerbate distrust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public remarks by celebrities reflect on associated organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: "Unfortunately, Tracy's comments reflect negatively on both '30 Rock' and NBC - two very all-inclusive and diverse organizations - and we have made it clear to him that this kind of behavior will not be tolerated." (NBC)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reputational impact: employers, shows, and networks may be judged by an artist's statements and may need to respond to uphold organizational values and protect stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess impact on coworkers and workplace dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Tina Fey: "I hope for his sake that Tracy's apology will be accepted as sincere by his gay and lesbian coworkers at '30 Rock,' without whom Tracy would not have lines to say, clothes to wear, sets to stand on, scene partners to act with, or a printed-out paycheck..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how offensive onstage remarks affect colleagues' sense of safety, morale, and professional relationships; production environments and coworkers have a stake in responses and remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severity can be judged by comparison and cultural norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Chris Rock's comments: initially defending Morgan as exercising foul/inappropriate speech, later saying "I get it that s--- wasn't called for and I don't support it at all," and comparing it to statements by Gary Busey or Flavor Flav.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observers often contextualize offensive remarks by comparing them to other public figures' behavior or to cultural norms; such comparisons influence perceptions of severity but should not be used to minimize harm to affected groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizations should state non-condonation of hate or violence
rubrics_metrics.description: "I speak for NBC and myself personally when I say we do not condone hate or violence of any kind... I am pleased to see Tracy Morgan apologizing..." (Bob Greenblatt/NBC)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions tied to performers may issue formal statements to reaffirm values, condemn hate speech, and clarify that freedom of expression is not a shield for violent or hateful rhetoric; such statements function as policy and public stance.
